title: The Prohibition on the Use of Force in International Law
seo_title: The Prohibition on the Use of Force in International Law
focus_keyword: prohibition on the use of force
cluster: Use of Force and International Humanitarian Law
excerpt: The prohibition on the use of force is one of the central rules of modern international law. This article explains how Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter restrains war, threats of force, intervention, territorial conquest, proxy violence, occupation, and coercive military action while preserving narrow exceptions for Security Council authorization and self-defense. It examines the meaning of territorial integrity and political independence, the definition of aggression, ICJ case law, cyber operations, drones, humanitarian intervention debates, collective security, and selective enforcement. By connecting doctrine, cases, and lawyer-facing analytical workflows, the article shows how use-of-force law remains indispensable while still vulnerable to great-power manipulation, alliance politics, evidentiary disputes, and unequal enforcement.
